behavior_problem_candidates.candidate: Behavior-conditioned hyperbolic Semantic-ID generation for next-item recommendation
evidence_basis: TIGER establishes autoregressive generation of the next item's Semantic ID from a user session (FULL_TEXT link; DOI 10.52202/075280-0452, arXiv:2305.05065).
HTSR establishes hyperbolic modeling of user, latest-item, and next-item behavior (ABSTRACT; DOI 10.1109/TCSS.2024.3409711).
behavior_problem_candidates.status: Synthesis/opportunity, not a verified existing paper combining all three axes.

evidence_basis: GNPR-SID reports IDs constructed from semantic and collaborative features and next-POI generation (ABSTRACT; DOI 10.1145/3711896.3736981).
Hyperbolic sequential recommendation papers model hierarchical behavioral structure, but the located evidence does not connect their geometry to Semantic-ID construction.
behavior_problem_candidates.status: Candidate gap; do not claim prior art already implements the three-way intersection.

behavior_problem_candidates.candidate: Jointly evaluate behavior fidelity and geometric hierarchy in generative next-item retrieval
evidence_basis: Generative retrieval provides a next-item generation setup; hyperbolic sequential methods motivate hierarchical behavior representations.
behavior_problem_candidates.status: Research question only; no located source verifies a unified evaluation/model.

limitations: No independently verified source located in this search explicitly combines user next-item behavior, hyperbolic geometry, and generative semantic item IDs in one method.

FULL_TEXT is reserved for the TIGER arXiv item because a public arXiv PDF/full-text endpoint is independently identified and the indexed abstract explicitly confirms the relevant method; the PDF was not downloaded for line-by-line audit in this run. Other works are conservatively labeled ABSTRACT even where a publisher PDF endpoint is listed.

Search evidence used Crossref/OpenAlex-indexed bibliographic records and abstracts plus canonical DOI/arXiv URLs. OpenAlex is an independent discovery/indexing source, not a substitute for publisher peer review or a full-text audit.
The set is a focused discovery sample, not an exhaustive systematic review. Search-engine/tool availability was limited; websearch calls were cancelled, so metadata/API discovery was used.

Some records have publication dates later than the current date indicated by this environment or may reflect indexing anomalies; do not rely on those records unless independently checked at the publisher/arXiv. They were excluded as support for the central overlap claim.

An abstract's omission of hyperbolic geometry or Semantic IDs does not prove the full paper omits the concept; the stated missing axis is limited to what was verified in the available abstract/record.
